newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AWB Report-Australia sees lower EU subsidies.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AWB Report-Australia sees lower EU subsidies.

text.p: European Union (EU) subsidies continued their downward trend, again heading towards their lows seen in October last year. In February, subsidies moved down to an average of 9.3 ECUs compared with 19 ECUs several weeks before, the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said in its weekly grain market report.

On the world market, the AWB said Tunisia purchased 125,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat for shipment April through June at US$166.96 - US$169.47 cost and freight. Japan purchased 180,000 tonnes of US hard redwinter wheat (HRW), hard redspring wheat and white wheats, Egypt bought 80,000 tonnes of HRW.
The Egyptian Government has indicated it has no plans to purchase further wheat prior to new crop Northern supplies coming onto the market in mid-May, the AWB said.
In February Egypt purchased approximately one million tonnes from a range of sources.
On the Australian market the AWB said Queensland sorghum harvest continued during the week with approximately 50 percent of the crop now in the bin.

Farmers continued to hold sorghum on farm and this has pushed prices higher with sorghum gaining a further five A$5 a tonne this week to trade about $145 delivered Brisbane and NSW sorghum trading around A$160 delivered Newcastle. The climb in south eastern feed grain (barley and triticale) prices since harvest has eased of late with larger parcels of grain coming onto the market and demanding steadying, the AWB said.

The AWB confirmed that its wheat shipments in the week ended March 21 totalled 572,922 tonnes, bringing exports so far this shipping year to 8.92 million tonnes. This is far ahead of the 6.06 million tonnes shipped at the same time last year.
